children.text: Part 2/4 — Rumi's levels are filled in: change any you saw differently and say why. Set the room levels yourself, with a reason.

children.name: r_C1
children.label: C1 — Quality of Questions…
children.description: Quality of Questions Asked by the Teacher. What kinds of questions the teacher asks, and whether they make children think. A closed question needs a yes/no or one-word answer, an open question needs a longer answer, and the strongest questions ask "why" and are followed up.

data-source.title: No questions, or answers given
data-source.description: No questions asked by the teacher, or asks the questions but gives the answers without waiting for students to answer.

data-source.title: Closed questions only
data-source.description: Teacher only asks closed questions with yes/no or one word answers.

data-source.title: 2+ open questions, waited
data-source.description: Teacher asks at least two open questions and waits for students to answer.

data-source.title: A 'why', then a follow-up
data-source.description: Teacher asks at least one question using 'why' and then follows up on the same child's answer (why? how do you know?).

data-source.title: N/A · Did not come up
data-source.description: What this indicator looks for did not come up in the lesson.

data-source.title: Couldn't tell
data-source.description: Use when the teacher's speech is missing or garbled for a large part of the lesson, so the questions cannot be made out.

children.label: Evidence
children.helper-text: C1 — what Rumi heard; edit if needed

children.name: r_C2
children.label: C2 — Helping when a child is…
children.description: Helping when a child is wrong. What the teacher does when a child's answer is wrong or incomplete: ignores it, says it is wrong, explains why, or helps the child fix it. It only applies when an answer was actually wrong.

data-source.title: Wrong answer ignored
data-source.description: A student gives a wrong answer and the teacher ignores it, or only repeats the same explanation in the same words.

data-source.title: Marked wrong, reason once
data-source.description: The teacher says the answer is wrong, or explains again, but gives the reason for the correction at most once.

data-source.title: Reason given 2+ times
data-source.description: At least two times, the teacher gives the reason for the correction and says what was right and what to change.

data-source.title: Child fixed it; new way tried
data-source.description: Beyond level 3, the teacher asks the student or another student to fix the answer, and tries a new way (a new example, a picture, smaller steps) if they are still stuck.

data-source.title: N/A · Did not come up
data-source.description: What this indicator looks for did not come up in the lesson.

data-source.title: Couldn't tell
data-source.description: Use when student answers are too garbled to tell whether any of them was wrong.

children.name: ev_C2
children.label: Evidence
children.helper-text: C2 — what Rumi heard; edit if needed

data-source.title: Took whoever answered
data-source.description: The teacher asks the whole class and takes whoever answers. No way of choosing who answers is heard: no name called before the question, no talking in pairs, no "everyone write".

data-source.title: Chose who answered once
data-source.description: The teacher uses a way of choosing who answers one time, for example calls a student by name, then goes back to taking whoever answers.

data-source.title: Chose who answered 2+ times
data-source.description: At least two times, the teacher uses a way of choosing who answers (a name called before the question, "tell your partner", "everyone write your answer", names picked at random).

data-source.title: 2+ named children answered
data-source.description: Beyond level 3, the teacher calls at least two different names to answer, and each is followed by an answer.

children.name: why_C3
children.label: Why this level
children.helper-text: What you saw, and how it fits the DC's evidence

children.name: r_C4
children.label: C4 — Children's choices
children.description: Children's choices. Whether children have a say in how the lesson goes: a real choice about how to do the work or explain it, the teacher taking up a child's idea, or a part of the lesson handed to them. Small choices (who goes first, which colour) are not real choices.

data-source.title: Teacher decided everything
data-source.description: The teacher decides everything and asks students for no choice or idea.

data-source.title: Small choices only
data-source.description: The teacher lets students choose only small things (who goes first, which colour), and decides everything about the learning.

data-source.title: A real choice or idea taken up
data-source.description: The teacher gives students at least one real choice about how to do the work or how to explain it, and lets them follow it, or takes up a child's idea.

data-source.title: Children led a part
data-source.description: Beyond level 3, the teacher hands a part of the lesson to students: a student or a group leads an activity, picks the method, or teaches the others.

data-source.title: N/A · Did not come up
data-source.description: What this indicator looks for did not come up in the lesson.

data-source.title: Couldn't tell
data-source.description: Use when the teacher's instructions for the tasks are missing or garbled.

children.name: ev_C4
children.label: Evidence
children.helper-text: C4 — what Rumi heard; edit if needed

data-source.title: Over 3 min, no signal
data-source.description: The class takes more than three minutes to change activity, and the teacher gives no clear signal.

data-source.title: Signal, 2-3 min
data-source.description: The teacher gives a signal, but the change still takes two to three minutes.

data-source.title: Under 2 min
data-source.description: The class changes activity in under two minutes of the teacher's signal.

data-source.title: Switched without being told
data-source.description: Beyond level 3, students already know what comes next and change without being told.

data-source.title: No switch
data-source.description: The class did not change activity.

children.name: why_C5
children.label: Why this level
children.helper-text: What you saw, and how it fits the DC's evidence

children.name: r_C6
children.label: C6 — Safe to be wrong
children.description: Safe to be wrong. Whether children feel safe to try and be wrong: how the teacher responds to their answers, whether praise is for effort or only for right answers, and whether mistakes are treated as useful.

data-source.title: Flat or dismissive
data-source.description: The teacher gives no encouragement. Replies to students are flat, dismissive, or only about the task.

data-source.title: Praise for right answers only
data-source.description: The teacher praises, but only for right answers or for doing as told, and only in general words.

data-source.title: Praised effort 2+ times
data-source.description: At least two times, the teacher praises a student's effort, trying, or thinking, not just a right answer.

data-source.title: Mistakes used, views invited
data-source.description: Beyond level 3, the teacher treats a wrong answer or an attempt as useful, and also invites other views.

data-source.title: N/A · Did not come up
data-source.description: What this indicator looks for did not come up in the lesson.

data-source.title: Couldn't tell
data-source.description: Use when the teacher's replies to student answers are missing or garbled for a large part of the lesson.

children.helper-text: C6 — what Rumi heard; edit if needed

data-source.title: No pair or group task
data-source.description: The teacher gives no pair or group task. Everyone works alone or as one class.

data-source.title: Groups, each works alone
data-source.description: The teacher puts students in pairs or groups, but each student does their own work.

data-source.title: Shared task, one product
data-source.description: The teacher gives a task that a group can only finish together, and says what the group must make.

data-source.title: Roles and report back
data-source.description: Beyond level 3, the teacher gives roles or turns inside the group, and asks the group to report back.

data-source.title: No group task
data-source.description: Everyone worked alone or as one class.

children.name: r_C8
children.label: C8 — Books and materials
children.description: Books and materials. Whether books, the board, charts or objects are used for learning, and by whom: only shown by the teacher, used by the children, or used by a child to explain while the teacher builds on what the child says.

data-source.title: No book or object mentioned
data-source.description: The teacher never mentions a book, the board, a chart, or any object or picture.

data-source.title: Shown only, not used
data-source.description: The teacher mentions a book, the board, or an object only to show or tell, and does not ask students to use it.

data-source.title: Children used them, linked
data-source.description: The teacher asks students to use a book, the board, or an object themselves, and says how it connects to the idea.

data-source.title: Child explained with them
data-source.description: Beyond level 3, the teacher asks a student to explain with the book, the chart or the object, and builds on what the student says.

data-source.description: What this indicator looks for did not come up in the lesson.

data-source.description: Use when the teacher's instructions are missing or garbled for a large part of the lesson.

cb_D2.__example__:
How many different children speak across the lesson, and whether children silent early on speak later.

05:10  "Ali, what do you think?"

Coach adds: how many different children spoke, and how many children who were quiet in the first half spoke in the second. The coach sets the final level with a written justification.

cb_D3.__example__:
Whether children talk to each other about the task, not only to the teacher: one child answers, agrees with or adds to what another said. At its strongest they give reasons to agree or disagree and reach one shared answer.

05:10  "Ali, what do you think?"

Coach adds: children talking to each other about the task that the recording did not pick up, mostly during pair and group work, and whether they gave reasons or reached a shared answer. The coach sets the final level with a written justification.

cb_D4.__example__:
Whether children dare to answer when they are not sure: they stay silent, answer only when sure, answer while unsure, or answer unasked and try again after a wrong answer. Only the trying counts, not whether the answer is right.

05:10  "Ali, what do you think?"

Coach adds: how children behave when they are unsure: whether they have a go or go quiet, put a hand up or wait for the teacher, and try again after a wrong answer. The coach sets the final level with a written justification.

children.name: r_D1
children.label: D1 — Children's reasoning
children.description: Children's reasoning. How deep children's answers are: one word, a longer answer that only repeats what was said, or an answer that shows reasoning in the child's own words (says why, compares, uses a rule on a new case, explains a choice, gives their own example).

data-source.title: One-word answers only
data-source.description: Students give only one-word answers or repeat a fact.

data-source.title: Longer, but only repeated
data-source.description: At least one answer, from any student, is longer than a phrase, but it only repeats what was already said or read, or finishes the teacher's sentence.

data-source.title: 2+ answers gave reasons
data-source.description: At least two answers, from any students, show reasoning in the child's own words: they say why, compare two things, use a rule on a new case, or explain a choice. Finishing the teacher's sentence, or repeating a reason the teacher already gave, does not count.

data-source.title: Child's own example or link
data-source.description: Beyond level 3, a student gives their own example, or links the idea to something else, that the teacher did not say first.

data-source.title: N/A · Did not come up
data-source.description: What this indicator looks for did not come up in the lesson.

data-source.title: 3-5 children
data-source.description: Three to five different children speak.

data-source.title: 6+, and 2+ quiet ones later

children.name: why_D2

children.helper-text: What you saw, and how it fits the DC's evidence

data-source.title: No child spoke to another
data-source.description: No student speaks to another student about the task.

data-source.title: Once
data-source.description: One time, a student answers and the teacher names a second child who agrees with the previous student's answer, or the student says I agree with her/him referring to the previously given answer by the student.

data-source.title: 2+ times
data-source.description: At least two times, a student answers, agrees with, or adds to what another student just said.

data-source.title: Reasons, one shared answer
data-source.description: Beyond level 3, students give a reason to agree or disagree with each other, and reach one shared answer.

data-source.title: No child-to-child talk
data-source.description: Do not score this indicator if there are no two Student lines in a row where students talk about the topic, and the teacher never names a second child to agree with a student's answer. It is then left out of the feedback.

children.name: why_D3
children.label: Why this level
children.helper-text: What you saw, and how it fits the DC's evidence

data-source.title: Silent or waited
data-source.description: When the teacher asks, students stay silent, say "I do not know", or wait for the teacher to give the answer.

data-source.title: Only answered when sure
data-source.description: Students answer only when they are sure. Nobody gives a half-sure answer; when unsure they say nothing.

data-source.title: Tried while unsure, 2+
data-source.description: At least two times, a student answers while clearly unsure, for example "Maybe...", "Should I say...?", or an answer that changes halfway.

data-source.title: Tried unasked or again
data-source.description: Beyond level 3, a student answers without being asked, or tries again after a wrong answer instead of giving up.

children.name: why_D4
children.label: Why this level
children.helper-text: What you saw, and how it fits the DC's evidence

children.name: r_D5
children.label: D5 — Children's own questions
children.description: Children's own questions. Whether children ask questions of their own: only about the task (which page, may I answer), or about the idea itself (how or why something works, a different case). Repeating the teacher's question or giving an unsure answer does not count.

data-source.title: No question of their own
data-source.description: No student asks the teacher a question of their own. An unsure answer ("Is it twelve?") or a student repeating the teacher's question ("Why?") does not count.

data-source.title: Task questions only
data-source.description: Students ask only questions about the task: which page, do we write this, is it homework, may I answer, or please say it again.

data-source.title: A question about the idea
data-source.description: Students ask at least one question about the idea itself: how or why something works, or what would happen in a different case.

data-source.title: 2+, one beyond the lesson
data-source.description: Beyond level 3, students ask at least two questions about the idea, and one of them is about something the teacher has not talked about in this lesson.

data-source.description: What this indicator looks for did not come up in the lesson.

children.name: r_F1
children.label: F1 — Accuracy of content
children.description: Accuracy of content. Whether what the teacher says about the subject is correct, and whether a wrong statement is corrected. Count something as wrong only when you are sure.

data-source.title: Wrong content left standing
data-source.description: The teacher says something wrong and leaves it, so students are left with wrong information. Count something as wrong only if you are sure; a word that may be a transcription or translation mistake does not count.

data-source.title: A slip not corrected
data-source.description: Mostly correct, but the teacher makes a small slip (a wrong rule or a wrong word) and does not correct it.

data-source.title: All correct
data-source.description: Everything the teacher says is correct. When not sure, the teacher says so and does not guess.

data-source.title: Warned of a common mistake
data-source.description: Beyond level 3, the teacher warns students about a common mistake before they make it.

data-source.title: N/A · Did not come up

data-source.title: Couldn't tell
data-source.description: Use when the teacher's speech is missing or garbled for a large part of the lesson, or the only possible errors may be transcription mistakes (a mis-heard number or term).

children.name: r_F3
children.label: F3 — Explaining why
children.description: Explaining why. Whether the teacher explains why a rule or step works, with a reason, an example or a picture, or only says how to do it. At its strongest, the teacher turns a child's question into a short lesson or asks the children to give the reason.

data-source.title: How only, no reason
data-source.description: The teacher only says how to do it, and gives no reason.

data-source.title: Some reasons, mostly rules
data-source.description: The teacher gives a reason now and then, but mostly asks students to remember the rule.

data-source.title: Explained why 2+ times
data-source.description: At least two times, the teacher explains why a rule or step works, with a reason, an example, or a picture.

data-source.title: Went further, or children did
data-source.description: Beyond level 3, the teacher turns a student's question into a short lesson that goes further, or asks the children to give the reason.
